narrativeSummary: May 20 was the session the market had been building toward for three weeks. Two forces that had been pulling in opposite directions — Iran war inflation and AI demand acceleration — both resolved in the same direction on the same day. The Iran breakthrough arrived first: three supertankers left the Strait of Hormuz with full cargoes under US military escort, the clearest physical evidence yet that the blockade is being lifted. Trump told reporters the administration was in the 'final stages' of negotiations with Iran. WTI crude fell 5.66% to $98.26 — back below $100 for the first time since early May. Brent fell 5.63% to $105.02. The Treasury market moved immediately: the 10Y yield fell from 4.63% (Monday's 52-week high) back toward 4.49% on the session, the biggest single-day yield decline since the April ceasefire. The equity rally was broad and decisive: Russell 2000 +2.44% led all indices as small caps — most hurt by the stagflation/rate-shock combo — reversed sharply. Energy was the only decliner (-2.08%) as the inflation trade unwound. Technology +2.11% and Consumer Discretionary +2.39% led. Target reported a blowout quarter before the open: EPS $1.71 vs $1.35 (26% beat), revenue $25.44B vs $24.64B — confirming that the consumer is not broken despite 3.8% CPI. TJX surged 6% on its own strong results. After the bell, Nvidia delivered the print Wall Street had been waiting for all year: $81.62B revenue (+85% YoY), data center $75.25B (+92%), EPS $1.87 vs $1.77, and — most critically — a Q2 guide of $91B versus the $87B consensus and $90B whisper number. Jensen Huang said 'demand has gone parabolic' and 'agentic AI has arrived — compute capacity is profits.' No H20 China revenue booked but sovereign AI programs from the Middle East, Asia, and Europe are the explicit offset, with the $50B China market still potential upside. CNBC noted the stock has slid on four of its last five earnings despite beats — but the $91B Q2 guide vs $87B consensus is the first time the guide has comprehensively exceeded even the whisper number. SpaceX IPO was formally set for June 12 at a $1.75T valuation — the largest IPO in history.

rateCurveRead: Yields fell sharply on May 20 as the three-supertanker Hormuz departure and Trump's 'final stages' comment removed the most acute energy inflation premium from the long end. The 10Y fell approximately 12bps from Monday's 52-week high of 4.63% to approximately 4.49% — the biggest single-day 10Y decline since the April ceasefire. The 30Y fell from 5.134% to approximately 5.08%, easing below 5.10% for the first time in a week. The 2Y held near 4.08%, as the near-term Fed path (Warsh June 17 hold) is still firmly priced. The 2/10 spread compressed to approximately +41bps from +50bps as the long end rallied faster than the short end — a classically bullish signal when driven by inflation resolution rather than growth concern. If 47,000 Samsung workers strike, HBM and DRAM supply tightens exactly as Nvidia guides to $91B in Q2 — requiring massive Blackwell memory deployment. Nvidia's $91B Q2 guide assumes no Samsung supply disruption. A strike materialising would create a supply-side challenge to the guide.

risks.title: Walmart Thursday — if consumer is broken at the lower-income level, Thursday becomes the reversal catalyst
risks.desc: Target's 26% EPS beat confirmed upper-income consumer resilience. But Target's customer is demographically different from Walmart's — higher income, more urban, younger. Walmart serves the lower-income consumer who is being most hurt by $4.56/gallon gas and 3.8% CPI. If Walmart misses on Thursday, the K-shaped consumer story inverts: upper-income resilient, lower-income stressed. The NY Fed's data showing lower-income households cutting gas consumption most is the early signal.

This is relevant because OpenAI is both a major Nvidia customer (consuming GPU compute) and the leading AI demand indicator. If OpenAI's revenue growth is below internal targets, the $20B cloud deal with Cerebras and the $852B valuation for its IPO require scrutiny. The WSJ report was a pre-market negative that the market ultimately absorbed — but the underlying concern about AI demand concentration in a single company (OpenAI) remains.

strategies.title: Long Nvidia Friday open — $91B Q2 guide is the first true blowout in 5 quarters
strategies.body: Nvidia's Q2 guide of $91B vs $87B consensus and $90B whisper is the first time in five quarters that the guide has exceeded even the buy-side whisper number. The prior four earnings saw beats with guides that merely met or slightly exceeded consensus — hence the 'sell the news' reaction. A $91B guide with 'demand gone parabolic' and 'agentic AI arrived' is the narrative upgrade needed. The Samsung risk and China zero revenue are the shadows on the print — but the magnitude of the $75.25B data center (+92% YoY) overwhelms both concerns. The template for a sustained post-earnings rally exists: this is structurally different from the prior four.

strategies.title: Long consumer discretionary — Target 26% beat + Iran energy relief = XLY trade
strategies.body: Target's 26% EPS beat confirmed the upper-income consumer is resilient. WTI below $100 means the lower-income consumer's energy burden eases — potentially unlocking Walmart's Q2. TJX +6% confirms value retail is also working. XLY +2.39% today was the best sector. If Walmart beats Thursday (the lower-income consumer test), the full consumer discretionary trade — from off-price to premium — is confirmed. The Iran energy deflation trade specifically benefits airlines, cruise, and auto as jet fuel and petrol prices fall.
strategies.trigger: Walmart Q1 beat Thursday AND WTI below $95 sustained

strategies.title: Pre-position SpaceX June 12 IPO — AI + space + defence is uniquely uncorrelated
strategies.body: SpaceX at $1.75T is the largest IPO in history, merging the world's most advanced rocket company with Musk's xAI. The AI + space + defence narrative has no listed equivalent — not Lockheed, not Boeing, not Nvidia. The Cerebras precedent (20x oversubscribed at IPO price, 68% first-day pop) suggests demand will be enormous. Risks: Tesla overhang (investors swap TSLA for SPCE), concentration in government contracts, Musk distraction factor. Approach: small initial allocation at IPO price, add on any first-week pullback below the open price.
strategies.trigger: SpaceX prospectus confirms $1.75T valuation AND Nasa/DoD contract pipeline quantified
